slides.title: IC Design Process: An Overview
points: Beginner's guide to VLSI technology.
Connects HDL code to silicon circuits.
Focuses on theoretical IC design flow.
Not a coding-specific course.

slides.title: What is an Integrated Circuit (IC)?
points: Electronic circuits on a tiny semiconductor plate.
Contains billions of transistors.
Can be Analog or Digital.
SoC: Entire system on a single chip.
slides.visual_hint: Magnified view of a silicon chip or a simple IC diagram

slides.title: Evolution of ICs: From SSI to VLSI
points: Early ICs (SSI) had few components.
Transistor count grew exponentially (MSI, LSI).
VLSI: Millions to billions of transistors.
Now, VLSI refers to all modern ICs.
slides.visual_hint: Timeline showing SSI, MSI, LSI, VLSI with increasing transistor counts

slides.title: Digital Circuit Fundamentals
points: All data is converted to binary (0s & 1s).
Circuits use switches (transistors) for voltage control.
Combinational: Output depends on current input.
Sequential: Output depends on input + past state (memory).
slides.visual_hint: Simple diagrams of a switch, or a logic gate

slides.title: Why Use Hardware Description Languages (HDLs)?
points: IC complexity grew beyond manual drawing.
HDLs describe circuit behavior at high level.
Abstract details from transistor level.
EDA tools convert HDL to fabrication mask.
slides.visual_hint: Flowchart: HDL code -> EDA Tools -> Fabrication Mask

slides.title: Verilog & SystemVerilog HDLs
points: Verilog: Developed 1984, IEEE standard 1995.
SystemVerilog: Extension of Verilog (2005).
Supports both design and verification.
Advanced features like Object-Oriented Programming.
